sectors.name: Technology
themes: US AI-infrastructure demand is a durable driver, with PLTR/MRVL/ALAB compounding on enterprise and edge-compute adoption, independent of Fed policy.
Indonesia's tech rally lags US by ~490bps, signaling local liquidity is chasing defensives—structural upside comes from digital-payment and e-commerce penetration, not hardware.
Supply-chain digitization (ZBRA, IT) is a multi-year theme as manufacturers automate tracking, a pull that persists despite global rate cycles.
sectors.ai: Buy US-listed AI/semis exposure (PLTR, MRVL, ALAB) into strength; Indonesia tech remains a laggard—rotate IDN capital to US names via local brokers, but trim PLTR on parabolic risk. Favor ZBRA/IT for logistics-automation spillover; avoid INTC turnaround noise.

Small-cap financials (HDFA, BEKS, IMJS) show high volatility and event-driven spikes, signaling speculative froth that institutional investors should avoid unless backed by clear earnings catalysts.

Accumulate ARTO on digital-payment structural tailwind. Trim BEKS/IMJS on weak fundamentals. Position for Q3 earnings: prefer banks with strong CASA and low NPL.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's nickel downstreaming policy continues to drive vertically integrated renewable and EV supply chain investments, benefiting TOBA's battery materials segment.
US solar and storage demand remains structurally strong despite rate volatility, as evidenced by broad-based gains in ENPH, SEDG, and FSLR, supporting global clean-tech sentiment.
Domestic EV adoption is accelerating in Indonesia, with VKTR's commercial vehicle focus capitalizing on fleet electrification mandates and infrastructure buildout.
sectors.ai: Buy the pullback in Indonesian renewables, led by TOBA and VKTR, as the sector's +0.97% local outperformance signals domestic policy tailwinds. US solar names (SEDG, ENPH, FSLR) confirm global demand strength. Accumulate TOBA for nickel-integrated EV battery exposure and VKTR for commercial EV adoption, targeting 15% upside over 3 months.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Ramadan and Lebaran consumption cycles are structurally boosting discretionary food and beverage volumes, favoring small-cap names with direct distribution to tier-2/3 Java markets.
Export-oriented processed food and agri-FMCG players (MERI, OASA) benefit from sustained global commodity demand and IDR weakness, providing durable earnings tailwinds.
Margin normalization in mid-cap staples (MBTO, ESTI) from lower input costs is a repeatable driver, as packaging and raw material inflation cools while pricing power persists.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap FMCG names riding rural demand and Ramadan restocking, but avoid chasing ENZO/PADA at +25%+ without volume confirmation. Rotate into mid-cap staples with margin recovery (MBTO, ESTI) and export-linked food processors (MERI, OASA) as IDX consumer breadth holds. Trim laggards into strength; watch for profit-taking after the 3-day run.

US biotech volatility (MRNA, IDXX) creates tactical entry points for Indonesia-focused investors seeking diversification, but requires strict position sizing.

Favor local diagnostics and pharma distributors with domestic revenue visibility, but trim names with US-linked volatility (MRNA, IDXX). Accumulate PRIM and IKPM for steady compounding; avoid chasing PRAY post-spike.

themes: Indonesia's e-commerce penetration and last-mile delivery demand continue to outpace GDP growth, structurally lifting 3PL and courier operators like GTSI and SOCI.

sectors.name: Property & Real Estate

Government-backed housing affordability schemes (FLPP, subsidy push) under Prabowo create a policy floor for mass-market developers, offsetting high mortgage-rate headwinds.
